metadata.title: DXL launches AI product discovery on Meta Muse via Commercetools

content.text:
Destination XL Group, a US apparel retailer specialising in big and tall men's clothing, is expanding into AI-powered shopping through Meta's artificial intelligence (AI) agent Muse.
Working alongside its digital commerce technology partner Commercetools, the retailer is using agentic commerce technology to link its menswear catalogue to AI-based shopping channels.
The integration enables DXL to provide its big and tall men's apparel listing – including pricing and availability details – directly through Muse.
Initially launched for product discovery in the US, the tool is designed to help consumers locate suitable merchandise through AI-driven searches.
DXL technology senior vice president Dave Potter said: "Our priority is making it easier for customers to find the right products, wherever they choose to shop. Our customers are already asking AI where to find clothes that fit. Connecting our catalogue to Muse through Commercetools means we can reach those customers as their shopping habits evolve."
According to Commercetools, DXL's shoppers frequently have distinct sizing and fit requirements, making AI-powered searches an additional avenue to pair them with relevant items.
Commercetools noted that introducing the catalogue to Muse allows the retailer to engage consumers during the research and discovery phases of their purchasing journey, creating another channel to draw prospective buyers, direct qualified traffic, and drive revenue growth as consumer habits shift toward AI.
It added that AI is becoming an initial starting point for shopping, presenting opportunities to reach consumers beyond conventional storefronts and search engines as part of DXL's wider strategy to engage customers wherever they choose to shop.
Nationwide, DXL operates nearly 300 stores and generates $435m in annual sales.
Its platform provider, Commercetools, describes itself as a digital commerce AI firm utilised by more than 500 global brands, retailers, and enterprise businesses.
Across the platform, these clients process more than $120bn in annualised gross merchandise value.
Commercetools CEO Doug McNary added: "As more consumers turn to AI for product recommendations, retailers have an opportunity to reach customers beyond traditional search engines and their own websites. With DXL, we are helping turn this shift in consumer behaviour into a new commercial opportunity."
"DXL launches AI product discovery on Meta Muse via Commercetools" was originally created and published by Retail Insight Network, a GlobalData owned brand.
